A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SMI/SUD are associated with a higher likelihood of transitions among employment statuses, with the exception of full-time employment.
SMI/SUD are associated with a higher risk of unemployment, but that once employed persons with SMI are more likely to remain so than persons without SMI.
SMI/SUD are associated with high rates of employment transitions and that full-time employment is the most stable employment state.

employment transitions are frequent for all groups, but persons with SMI are at a distinct disadvantage.
employment is a dynamic process that is influenced by the presence of a mental disorder.
